([[Woodland Hills, California]]) | college = *[[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] (2010–2011) *[[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] (2012–2014) *[[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2014–2015) | draft_year = 2015 | career_start = 2015 | career_end = 2016 | career_number = 31 | career_position = [[Shooting guard]] | years1 = 2015–2016 | team1 = [[Idaho Stampede]] | years2 = {{nbay|2015|end}} | team2 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Mountain West]] (2014) | bbr = dejeabr01 }} '''Bryce Alexander Dejean-Jones''' (August 21, 1992 – May 28, 2016) was an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Iowa State Cyclones|Iowa State University]] after stints with [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], and played professionally for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was fatally shot on May 28, 2016, making him the first active NBA player to die since 2007. ==High school career== Dejean-Jones attended [[View Park Preparatory High School]] for two years, then transferred to and graduated from [[William Howard Taft Charter High School]] in the [[Woodland Hills, Los Angeles|Woodland Hills]] section of Los Angeles. As a senior in 2009–10, he averaged 16.9 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.6 steals and made 56.8 percent of his shots, including 49.3 percent from beyond the arc in leading the Toreadors to the L.A. City Section final and third round of the Division I state playoffs.{{cite news|url=http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/bryce_dejean_jones_797957.html|title=#13 Bryce Dejean-Jones|work=UNLVrebels.com|access-date=August 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305014408/http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/bryce_dejean_jones_797957.html|archive-date=March 5, 2016|url-status=dead}} ==College career== Dejean-Jones began his college career with [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], appearing in 18 of 34 games as a freshman and starting in each of the Trojans' first 10 games. In 20.6 minutes per game, he averaged 7.6 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 37.9 percent from the field and 34.5 percent from three-point range, scoring in double figures seven times, including a career-high 21 points against [[2010–11 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|New Mexico State]]. After his freshman season, Dejean-Jones transferred to [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], redshirting as a sophomore. As a redshirted sophomore in 2012–13, he was named the [[Mountain West]] Preseason Co-Newcomer of the Year prior to the start of the season, going on to appear in all 35 games, starting 29. He was third in scoring for the Runnin' Rebels with 10.3 points per game, third in steals and assists with 0.9 and 2.3 per game respectively, and fourth in rebounds with 4.4 rebounds per game, leading his team in scoring five times and in rebounding twice. He made his debut on November 12, 2012, scoring 15 points, including hitting 3-of-4 three-pointers, in a win over [[2012–13 Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball team|Northern Arizona]] which was the first of 18 total games of scoring in double figures. He also dished out a career-high six assists in three different games, and exploded for a career-high 22 points on 7-of-11 shooting in a 76–75 win over [[2012–13 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] to help UNLV earn its best non-conference road win of the season. On February 9, 2014, he grabbed a career-high nine rebounds in a home win over [[2013–14 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico]] and made a career-high five three-pointers as part of a team-leading 19-point effort in the MW tournament's championship game on March 16, also against the Lobos. Five days later, he made his NCAA tournament debut against Cal, scoring a team-high 15 points in a 64–61 loss. In 2014, Dejean-Jones transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] to play under coach [[Fred Hoiberg]]. Dejean-Jones played in 33 games during the 2014–15 season, starting 21, averaging 10.5 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 steals, while shooting a career-best 47.6 percent from the field. He scored in double figures 17 times and earned CBSSports.com National Player of the Week honors after scoring a season-high 27 points in ISU's win against nationally ranked [[2014–15 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]]. In that game, he was 8-for-8 from the field, becoming just the fifth player in school history with at least eight field goal attempts in a game without a miss. In his Cyclone debut, he recorded his first career double-double, finishing with 20 points and 11 rebounds against [[2014–15 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]], and just missed a triple-double against [[2014–15 Lamar Cardinals basketball team|Lamar]], scoring 12 points to go along with 10 rebounds and a career-high eight assists. He helped the Cyclones win the [[2015 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|2015 Big 12 tournament]].{{cite news|url=http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=209511174|title=#13 |access-date= 1 November 2017 }} ==Professional career== ===Idaho Stampede (2015–2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Dejean-Jones joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] in Las Vegas, averaging 12.8 points in six games.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-bryce-dejean-jones|title=Pelicans Sign Bryce Dejean-Jones|work=NBA.com|date=August 20, 2015|access-date=August 21, 2015}} On August 20, 2015, he signed with the Pelicans, but was later waived by the team on October 24 after appearing in seven preseason games.{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive Jeff Adrien, Bryce Dejean-Jones, Bo McCalebb|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-jeff-adrien-bryce-dejean-jones-bo-mccalebb|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2015|access-date=October 24, 2015}} On December 13, he was acquired by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|title=Stampede Acquire Bryce Dejean-Jones off Waivers|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5079941|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 13, 2015|access-date=December 13, 2015}} He made his professional debut on December 19 in a 117–107 win over the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], recording 15 points, three rebounds, four assists and one steal in 21 minutes of action.{{cite web|title=Williams, Warriors Come up Short to Stampede|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151219/IDASCW/|access-date=December 19, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2016|archive-date=February 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160205021841/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151219/idascw/|url-status=dead}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2016)=== On January 21, 2016, Dejean-Jones signed a 10-day contract with the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=Pelicans Sign Bryce Dejean-Jones to 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-bryce-dejean-jones-10-day-contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 21, 2016|access-date=January 21, 2016}} On January 28, in his fourth game for the team, Dejean-Jones started at shooting guard in place of the injured [[Tyreke Evans]]. In 34 minutes of action, he recorded 14 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 steals and 1 block, helping the Pelicans defeat the [[Sacramento Kings]] 114–105.{{cite web|title=Anderson scores 36, leads Pelicans past Kings, 114–105|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160128/SACNOP/gameinfo.html|access-date=January 29, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504040408/http://www.nba.com/games/20160128/SACNOP/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 4, 2016|url-status=dead}} On February 1, he signed a second 10-day contract,{{cite web|title=Pelicans Sign Bryce Dejean-Jones to Second 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-bryce-dejean-jones-second-10-day-contract|access-date=February 1, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2016}} and continued to start for the Pelicans due to Evans' injury. On February 4, he had a career-best game with 17 points and 9 rebounds in a 99–96 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Resurgent Kobe Bryant leads Lakers past Pelicans, 99–96|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160204/LALNOP/gameinfo.html|access-date=February 5, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426164950/http://www.nba.com/games/20160204/LALNOP/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 26, 2016|url-status=dead}} On February 19, he signed a three-year deal with the Pelicans.{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Bryce Dejean-Jones|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-bryce-dejean-jones-0|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016}}{{cite news|title=The Pelicans and rookie starter Bryce Dejean-...|url=https://twitter.com/ShamsCharania/status/700499306294468609|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=Twitter|date=February 19, 2016}} A week later, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing successful surgery to repair a right wrist fracture.{{cite news|title=Bryce Dejean-Jones Undergoes Successful Surgery|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/bryce-dejean-jones-undergoes-successful-surgery|access-date=February 26, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2016}} ==Personal life== Dejean-Jones was the son of KC and Franchesca Jones, and had four brothers and two sisters. He graduated from UNLV with a degree in sociology and pursued a master's degree in family and consumer sciences – youth development. He had one daughter, Allicsia DeJean. ==Death== On May 28, 2016, Dejean-Jones was killed when he was shot after kicking open the locked front door and locked bedroom door of a Camden Belmont Dallas apartment which he mistakenly thought belonged to his girlfriend.{{cite web | title=Pelicans guard Bryce Dejean-Jones went to wrong apartment, CNN reports | work= nola.com | url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/05/pelicans_guard_bryce_dejean-jo_1.html |access-date=May 28, 2016}}{{cite web | title=Agent: Pelicans' Dejean-Jones in 'wrong place' when shot| work= sentinelandenterprise.com | url=http://www.sentinelandenterprise.com/ci_29954539/pelicans-dejean-jones-killed-after-going-wrong-apartment |access-date=May 29, 2016}}{{cite web | title=NBA guard killed after mistakenly entering stranger's apartment | work= nypost.com | date= May 28, 2016 | url=https://nypost.com/2016/05/28/pelicans-guard-bryce-dejean-jones-dead-at-23/ |access-date=May 28, 2016}}{{cite web |date=May 29, 2016 |title=NBA's Bryce Dejean-Jones killed after going to wrong apartment in Dallas |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/ct-nba-bryce-dejean-jones-death-spt-20160528-story.html |access-date=January 20, 2024 |work=chicagotribune.com}} He was visiting his girlfriend, who lived on the floor above, for their daughter's first birthday. Dejean-Jones intended to re-enter her apartment after leaving to take a walk following an argument with her,{{cite web | title=Pelicans guard Dejean-Jones shot and killed after accessing wrong Dallas apartment | work= [[Fox News]] | date= May 28, 2016 | url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/pelicans-guard-dejean-jones-shot-and-killed-after-accessing-wrong-dallas-apartment |access-date=May 29, 2016}} but instead went to another apartment one floor below his girlfriend's apartment on the fourth floor. At about 3:20 a.m., Dejean-Jones forced open the front door of the third-floor apartment. While shouting for his girlfriend,{{Cite news |last=Joseph |first=Adi |date=2016-05-28 |title=Pelicans guard Bryce Dejean-Jones dies at 23 years old |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/bryce-dejean-jones-death-pelicans-new-orleans-iowa-state-usc-unlv-age/c9c03wnkleen12znthw25uani |access-date=January 20, 2024 |work=Sporting News}}{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/marcjspearsespn/status/736736581906632705|title=Shout for girlfriend|last=Spears|first=Marc|date=May 28, 2016|website=Twitter|access-date=June 14, 2017}} Dejean-Jones approached and kicked open the bedroom door within the apartment. The resident, who had been sleeping, thought that the person breaking in intended to harm him, so he proceeded to retrieve and fire a handgun in self defense at Dejean-Jones through the bedroom door, striking him in the abdomen.{{cite web | title=Bryce Dejean-Jones shot dead while screaming for girlfriend in apartment, NBA concludes | work= nola.com | url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/05/bryce_dejean-jones_shot_dead_w.html |access-date=May 29, 2016}}{{Cite Life|last=Pearlman|first=Jeff|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=2017-05-16|language=en-US}} Dejean-Jones, at the age of 23, was pronounced dead at a Dallas hospital.{{cite web|title=Police: Pelicans
